root_cause: This is a known, previously-recorded flaky test (pattern a284d27dfee44614, now at 5 occurrences across unrelated PRs since 2026-08-27). TestKerasLSTM::test_keras_lstm_flags_float32 uses dropout (0.1, 0.3) on an LSTM layer, which TF implements with internal, framework-controlled random masking that is not bit-reproducible against the CPU plugin's reference LSTM evaluation. The resulting output differs from the TF framework reference by a small but non-zero margin (third decimal place, e.g. -1.07 vs -0.99), occasionally exceeding the test's comparison tolerance. The failure is not linked to the current PR's Histc-17 changes (none of PR #39286's changed files touch LSTM/RNN code paths), confirming it is an environment/test-tolerance flakiness rather than a regression introduced by this PR.
reproduction_steps: Run locally: `pytest install/tests/layer_tests/tensorflow2_keras_tests/test_tf2_keras_lstm.py::TestKerasLSTM::test_keras_lstm_flags_float32 -k flags_float32 --device CPU` repeatedly; failure is intermittent and dropout-seed dependent, so multiple runs may be needed to reproduce.
recommended_actions: Increase the comparison tolerance (eps/rtol) for TestKerasLSTM::test_keras_lstm_flags_float32 when dropout is enabled, or mark the dropout-enabled LSTM parametrization as xfail/flaky given 5 recorded recurrences.
Consider disabling dropout during TF reference generation (model.trainable=False / dropout rate 0 at inference) so the comparison is deterministic.
Track ticket for a permanent fix instead of relying on reruns indefinitely; the rerun pattern has already masked 5 occurrences.
prevention_strategies: Add tolerance scaling or deterministic-mode handling for any test that exercises dropout-containing layers at inference time, since TF's dropout behavior during evaluation should be a no-op but numerically interacts with random-state initialization; review the test's `ir_version`/precision thresholds for LSTM+dropout parametrizations specifically.
historical_context: Recorded 5 times since 2026-08-27 (first occurrence) across unrelated PRs (#37611, #37654, #38168, #39121, and now #39286); also a related but distinctly-signed prior pattern (134f01149f41adcc, 3 occurrences 2026-06-26 to 2026-07-01) with the same symptom but different normalization. Always resolves via workflow rerun; no code fix has been merged yet.
